name: n_in_follow_up_at_interval_start_bw
info: Number of Lexis subjects in follow-up at the start of a follow-up time scale interval.

name: n_entered_late_during_interval_bw
info: Number of Lexis subjects who entered a follow-up time scale interval late.

name: n_left_early_during_interval_bw
info: Number of Lexis subjects who left a follow-up time scale interval early.

name: n_at_risk_eff_bw
info: Effective number of subjects at risk. Whereas in the Kaplan-Meier (product-limit) estimator of survival we simply estimate the conditional survival probabilities as `n_events / n_at_risk` at each event time point, in the actuarial approach we estimate the conditional survival probabilities of follow-up time intervals such as `]0, 0.1]`. Using the number at risk at the start of the interval is problematic because subjects may enter late, leave early, or both. We adjust our number at risk in each of these special cases to arrive out our effective number.

name: n_events_bw
info: Number of events, i.e. the total number of all kinds of transitions.

name: n_events_exp_e2_bw
info: Number of expected events according to the Ederer II method. Well, there is only one formula for the expected number of events, `h_exp * t_at_risk`, but this name is reserved for the Ederer II method and is used with observed data (as opposed to extrapolated data according to the Ederer I method).

name: n_events_pp_bw
info: The same `n_events` but with Pohar Perme weighting.

name: n_events_pp_double_weighted_bw
info: The same as `n_events` but with Pohar Perme weighting where the weights are squared.

name: n_events_exp_pp_bw
info: The number of expected events with Pohar Perme weighting.

name: n_at_risk_eff_pp_bw
info: The same as `n_at_risk_eff` but with Pohar Perme weighting.

name: t_at_risk_pp_bw
info: The same as `t_at_risk` but with Pohar Perme weighting.

name: n_events_[x, y]_bw
info: The number of transitions from `x` to `y`.
